claims.text: Existing multimodal agents often select visual experts using textual outputs or heuristics and lack quantitative criteria for deciding when visual assistance is needed or which expert to invoke.
DnR reformulates a question into concrete visual queries, grounds each query with a CLIP-based model, and averages the resulting spatial relevance maps.

The utilization metric combines semantic change after masking relevant regions with prediction stability after masking irrelevant regions; its adaptive weighting uses relevance-map entropy and contrast.
Expert boxes, masks, or depth maps are rendered onto the original image for re-querying through the existing vision encoder without architectural modification.
DnR recomputes utilization for expert-rendered candidates using the original masks, selects the largest positive improvement over the draft, and retains the draft if no expert improves utilization.

The experiments use LLaMA-3-70B for query decomposition, CLIPSeg for grounding, and GroundingDINO, SAM, DepthAnything, and mDETR as visual experts; utilization uses 16 stochastic masks per image, with masking ratios 0.25 for Top-k and 0.75 for Bottom-k.

The comprehensive evaluation covers 16 multimodal benchmarks across VQA, image captioning, visual reasoning, knowledge VQA, and comprehensive evaluation, using dataset subsets, GRAY rendering, and Hybrid masking.
Hallucination evaluation uses HaloQuest, MMHal-Bench, VizWiz, and COCO Caption with highlight rendering; ChatGPT 4o-mini categorizes responses as Hallucination, Misperception, Grounded, or Correct.
Table 1 reports IDEFICS VQAv2 performance increasing from 37.8 to 47.85, while its VizWiz performance decreases from 43.33 to 36.67.
Qwen2.5-VL captioning performance on Flickr decreases from 57.3 to 55.9 after DnR.
Table 2 reports Qwen2.5-VL's hallucination proportion on COCO Caption decreasing from 48.24% to 26.13%.
For PaliGemma, policy-driven selection reduces average computational cost by 70.39%; VQAv2 accuracy changes from 75.2% under exhaustive selection to 74.9%, and COCO CIDEr changes from 144.7 to 143.5.

Rendering styles and parameters require dataset- and model-specific tuning; utilization levels and changes vary across datasets, architectures, and inputs, and Hybrid masking remains a heuristic sensitive to masking ratio, rendering style, and expert setup.
DnR cannot recover conceptual facts absent from the model; the paper characterizes its benefit as improving access to existing knowledge rather than augmenting knowledge.

The paper contributes a quantitative visual-utilization criterion for selecting and incorporating visual experts, a rendering interface that integrates experts without retraining, and a learned selector that approximates exhaustive expert evaluation.
